skill.name: haskell-pro
skill.description: Advanced Haskell guidance for type-safe architecture, pure design, concurrency, performance, project structure, parsing, and property-based testing.
skill.summary: Build maintainable Haskell with strong types, pure boundaries, and practical verification.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a documentation path in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only Haskell guidance with no executable code, network access, credential access, or prompt-injection text found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown backticks to format a referenced documentation path, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md contains prose instructions only, with no executable command invocation.

content.value_statement: Advanced Haskell work often needs careful type design, IO boundaries, and verification. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward idiomatic, testable Haskell solutions.
actual_capabilities: Recommends expressive Haskell types, including newtypes, GADTs, type families, and phantom types.
Designs pure functional architecture with clear IO boundaries and total functions.
Explains concurrency approaches using STM, async, lightweight threads, and exception-safe combinators.
Suggests performance improvements with strictness, profiling, and fusion.
Improves Cabal or Stack project layout, dependency hygiene, parsing, and test strategy.
limitations: It does not run compilers, tests, profilers, or package managers by itself.
It depends on the project details and constraints provided in the prompt.
It cannot replace validation in the target GHC, Cabal, or Stack environment.
It is scoped to Haskell and related engineering workflows.

use_cases.title: Type-Safe Domain Modeling
use_cases.description: Model business rules with newtypes, algebraic data types, and safer constructors before implementation.

use_cases.title: Functional Architecture Review
use_cases.description: Review module boundaries, IO isolation, effect design, and error handling for a growing Haskell project.

use_cases.title: Production Readiness Planning
use_cases.description: Plan concurrency, performance checks, dependency hygiene, and property-based testing for a service release.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Haskell function for safer types, total behavior, and clearer names. Explain changes in plain language: [paste function]

prompt_templates.title: Design a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Haskell module for [domain]. Include key types, pure functions, IO boundaries, and test ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Cabal or Stack project structure. Recommend module organization, dependency cleanup, build settings, and verification steps: [paste tree]

prompt_templates.title: Engineer a High-Assurance System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a high-assurance Haskell approach for [system]. Use strong invariants, concurrency safety, parsing strategy, performance checks, and property tests.

output_examples.input: I need safer types for user IDs and order IDs.
output: A recommendation to use separate newtypes for each identifier.
A constructor plan that prevents mixing unrelated identifiers.
Property-test ideas for parsing and serialization.

output_examples.input: My service has STM queues and async workers.
output_examples.output: A review of worker lifecycle, cancellation behavior, exception handling, and shutdown flow with suggested verification steps.

output_examples.input: Our parser accepts partial input and gives unclear errors.
output_examples.output: A plan for Megaparsec parser structure, better error reporting, total result handling, and focused test cases.

best_practices: Share compiler errors, module boundaries, and constraints when asking for design help.
Ask for explicit type signatures, invariants, and total alternatives to partial functions.
Validate recommendations with GHC, tests, benchmarks, and project-specific review.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without sharing goals, inputs, and success criteria.
Do not accept advanced language extensions unless their purpose is clear.
Do not skip local compilation, property tests, or performance checks for generated designs.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, review, and improve Haskell code using strong types, pure functions, tests, and practical architecture.

faq.question: Can it write complete Haskell modules?
faq.answer: It can draft module plans and code-oriented guidance, but outputs should be compiled and tested locally.

faq.question: Does it support Stack and Cabal?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discuss project structure, dependency hygiene, and build configuration for Stack or Cabal workflows.

faq.question: Can it debug compiler errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the error text, relevant signatures, and surrounding context.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for step-by-step explanations and avoid advanced extensions until the basics are clear.

faq.question: Does it run Haskell tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only unless the host agent has separate tool access and permission.
